system.name: FREE (ViT-g OPT2.7B)
system.one_liner: Early exits for vision-language models, each exit a transformer layer trained adversarially to mimic the final layer, for faster inference.

content.variant_note: nine rounded chat cards in a 3 by 3 grid, each a photo with VQA exchanges or a caption, answer words recoloured by the layer that predicts them
content.argues: Most words of a caption or answer are easy and can be predicted at early layers, so early exits can speed up inference without hurting the outputs.
content.subject: Nine photos with questions and the model's answers, whose words are coloured by the layers at which they are predicted.

elements.name: chat cards
elements.role: nine examples, each holding a photo and one or two exchanges, or a captioning prompt
elements.drawn_as: large rounded rectangles with a thin black outline in a 3 by 3 grid

elements.name: user question bubbles
elements.role: questions such as 'How many dogs are there?' or the captioning prompt 'A photo of'
elements.drawn_as: right-aligned light-blue rounded bubbles with a thin outline, a person icon at their right

elements.name: model answer boxes
elements.role: FREE's answers such as 'Looks like 2.' or 'A golden retriever dog laying down next to a pool in the backyard.'
elements.drawn_as: left-aligned white rounded boxes with a thin outline, a robot icon at their left, words in red, green or black

elements.name: word colours red, green, black
elements.role: tells at which layers each word of an answer is predicted: red layers 1-12, green layers 13-24, black layers 25-32
elements.drawn_as: recoloured words inside the answer boxes; the key is only in the caption

relations.what: the question is about the photo above it
each answer replies to the question above it
the colour of a word says how deep the model needs to go to predict it

panels.shows: dog wearing a mask: how many dogs, are they both wearing hats
woman with a vulture: what is in the photo, are there other animals
steam train: is it a toy train, how many cars
planes seen through an airport window: what is in the image, is anything moving
traffic light against the sky: which lights are on, is the sky clear
bird in a flowerpot: what is the bird doing, is the apple healthy
dog by a pool: caption completing 'A photo of'
zebra in snow: caption completing 'A photo of'
plane taking off: caption completing 'A photo of'

pictures.what: nine photographs: a dog wearing a mask, a woman with a vulture, a steam train, planes seen through an airport window, a traffic light against the sky, a bird in a flowerpot, a golden retriever by a pool, a zebra in snow, a plane taking off
pictures.treatment: unframed rectangular photos of about 52-63 x 33-47 pt at the top of each card, slightly right of centre

icons.depicts: simple robot head with an antenna

examples.what: six short visual question answering exchanges, e.g. 'Is this a toy train?' answered 'No.' and 'Which lights are on?' answered 'Red.'
examples.form: blue question bubbles over white answer boxes with recoloured words

examples.what: three captions generated from the prompt 'A photo of', e.g. 'A zebra standing in snowy field with a wall behind it.'
examples.form: prompt bubble over a white answer box with recoloured words

idioms.drawn_as: right-aligned light-blue user bubbles with a person icon and left-aligned white answer boxes with a robot icon, one per turn
rounded card with a photo, one or two question-answer turns and recoloured answer words instead of ticks and crosses
plain robot-head line icon beside each answer

content.reading_order: Row by row from the top-left card; inside a card from the photo down through question and answer turns.

layout.arrangement_note: Nine equal rounded cards in three rows of three, separated by whitespace. Each card stacks a photo at the top, then question bubbles aligned to the right with person icons and answer boxes aligned to the left with robot icons; the last three cards hold a single captioning prompt and answer.

palette.used_for: words predicted at the initial layers 1-12 (easy)
a lighter green used for some intermediary words

style.stroke: 0.25 pt black outlines on cards, bubbles and answer boxes
style.font: sans (Arial) 5 pt only, words recoloured red, green or black

encoding.color_means: word colour in an answer = depth at which the token is predicted: red easy (layers 1-12), green intermediate (13-24), black hard (25-32); light blue = user question
encoding.line_style_means: thin black outlines only; no line style carries meaning
encoding.shape_means: large rounded rectangle = one example; right-aligned blue bubble with a person icon = the user; left-aligned white box with a robot icon = the model
encoding.marker_means: no numbers or letters; the word colour is the only mark
encoding.emphasis: the recoloured words inside the answers, and a photo at the top of every card
reusable_patterns: 3 by 3 grid of rounded chat cards each topped by a photo
right-aligned blue user bubbles with a person icon over left-aligned white answers with a robot icon
recolouring single words of a generated answer to show a per-token property such as the exit layer
captioning examples shown as the prompt 'A photo of' completed by the model
unframed photo at the top of each card
weaknesses: the colour key (red, green, black as exit depth) is only in the caption, not in the figure
the person icon sits beside the photo in some cards and not in others
red against green is hard to tell apart for some readers

own: nine photos with the model's real answers and their per-token exit layers

objects: photos on top of the cards
white answer boxes with coloured words

lessons.what_to_learn: Show a token-level property, such as the layer at which a word is decided, by recolouring words in real chat examples inside a uniform grid of photo-plus-dialogue cards.
lessons.suits: Qualitative-result teasers for models with per-token or per-step behaviour (early exit, speculative decoding, confidence) over VQA or captioning examples.

summary: FREE adds early exits to vision-language models, training each exit adversarially so that a small transformer layer mimics the final layer. Figure 1 is a 3 by 3 gallery of rounded chat cards from FREE ViT-g OPT2.7B. Each card has a photo on top (a dog, a vulture, a steam train, planes, a traffic light, a bird, a pool, a zebra, a plane), user questions as light-blue bubbles with a person icon and the model's answers as white boxes with a robot icon. Words in the answers are recoloured by the layer at which they are predicted: red for easy tokens in layers 1 to 12, green for layers 13 to 24 and black for layers 25 to 32. The key appears only in the caption.
